faq.q: What does attitude of gratitude mean?
faq.a: It means making appreciation your default way of seeing life. Instead of focusing only on what’s missing, you regularly notice what is good and already present.

faq.q: Why is gratitude called the highest attitude?
faq.a: Because it lifts other qualities with it, like patience, generosity, and contentment. It can’t always change your circumstances, but it changes how you experience them.

faq.q: How do I develop an attitude of gratitude?
faq.a: Start small and stay consistent. Try writing three good things each night with why they mattered, thanking someone specifically each week, and attaching moments of thanks to daily habits.

faq.q: Is gratitude the same as ignoring problems?
faq.a: No. Gratitude sits alongside real problems and feelings rather than replacing them. You can be thankful for what’s good and still work on what’s hard.

faq.q: What if my gratitude practice feels fake?
faq.a: Get more specific and vary what you notice so it doesn’t become a script. Keep it private if performing it feels hollow, and let the feeling follow the habit.

faq.q: Can I practice gratitude during a difficult time?
faq.a: Yes, but keep it very small. Focusing on one steady thing, like a supportive friend or a quiet moment, is enough on hard days.
